blocks.html:
This method defines indices on the data model. An index can be on multiple columns
and have conditions.

children.name: name
children.description:
The name of the index. If not provided,
Medusa generates the name.

children.name: unique
children.description:
When enabled, a unique index is created on the specified
properties.

children.name: on
children.description: The list of properties to create the index on.

children.name: where
children.description: Conditions to restrict which records are indexed.

children.name: type
children.description: The type of the index. (e.g: GIN)

types.name: indexes
types.description:
This method defines indices on the data model. An index can be on multiple columns
and have conditions.
types.example: An example of a simple index:import { model } from "@medusajs/framework/utils" const MyCustom = model.define("my_custom", { id: model.id(), name: model.text(), age: model.number() }).indexes([ { on: ["name", "age"], }, ]) export default MyCustomTo add a condition on the index, use the`where`option:import { model } from "@medusajs/framework/utils" const MyCustom = model.define("my_custom", { id: model.id(), name: model.text(), age: model.number() }).indexes([ { on: ["name", "age"], where: { age: 30 } }, ]) export default MyCustomThe condition can also be a negation. For example:import { model } from "@medusajs/framework/utils" const MyCustom = model.define("my_custom", { id: model.id(), name: model.text(), age: model.number() }).indexes([ { on: ["name", "age"], where: { age: { $ne: 30 } } }, ]) export default MyCustomIn this example, the index is created when the value of`age`doesn't equal`30`.
